Build two features for Rankora at `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora`: **Custom Pipeline Stages** + **Structured Evaluation Scorecards**.

Read CLAUDE.md first. Then read these files before coding:
- `src/hooks/useStageTracker.ts` — current hardcoded stages
- `src/components/KanbanBoard.tsx` — current kanban using STAGE_ORDER
- `src/components/JobDetailView.tsx` — where kanban is integrated
- `src/pages/SharedPortal.tsx` — uses stage labels
- `src/components/candidate/CandidateNotesPanel.tsx` — notes pattern
- `src/hooks/useCandidateNotes.tsx` — hook pattern to follow
- `src/components/CandidateDetailSheet.tsx` — candidate detail panel

---

## Feature A: Custom Pipeline Stages

### Problem
Stages are hardcoded as `STAGE_ORDER = ["applied", "screened", "interview", "offer", "hired"]` with "rejected" as special. Users can't customize their hiring pipeline.

### DB Migration — `supabase/migrations/20260408800000_custom_stages_and_scorecards.sql`

```sql
-- Custom stages per team
CREATE TABLE public.pipeline_stages (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  color text NOT NULL DEFAULT '#6366f1',
  sort_order integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  is_default boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_pipeline_stages_team ON public.pipeline_stages(team_id, sort_order);
ALTER TABLE public.pipeline_stages ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "Team members can view stages"
  ON public.pipeline_stages FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));

CREATE POLICY "Team admins can manage stages"
  ON public.pipeline_stages FOR ALL TO authenticated
  USING (public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id));

-- Seed default stages for existing teams
INSERT INTO public.pipeline_stages (team_id, name, color, sort_order, is_default)
SELECT t.id, s.name, s.color, s.sort_order, true
FROM public.teams t
CROSS JOIN (VALUES
  ('Applied', '#64748b', 0),
  ('Screened', '#3b82f6', 1),
  ('Interview', '#8b5cf6', 2),
  ('Offer', '#f59e0b', 3),
  ('Hired', '#10b981', 4)
) AS s(name, color, sort_order);
```

### New hook — `src/hooks/usePipelineStages.tsx`

```typescript
export function usePipelineStages(teamId: string | null) {
  // Fetch custom stages for the team
  // Return: { stages, isLoading, createStage, updateStage, deleteStage, reorderStages }
  // Stages include a synthetic "Rejected" stage at the end (always present, not deletable)
  // Fallback: if no custom stages, return DEFAULT_STAGES constant
}
```

- Query `pipeline_stages` table ordered by `sort_order`
- Always append a synthetic "Rejected" entry (special stage, not stored in DB)
- CRUD mutations for stages
- Realtime subscription

### Stage Manager UI — `src/components/PipelineStageManager.tsx`

Add this to the Team page or as a collapsible section in job settings.

Props: `teamId: string`

Features:
- List of current stages with: name, color dot, up/down reorder, edit, delete
- Add stage: name input + color picker (simple hex input or preset palette)
- Cannot delete default stages or "Rejected"
- Cannot have fewer than 2 stages
- Save updates sort_order

### Update useStageTracker.ts

Instead of hardcoded `STAGE_ORDER`, fetch stages from `usePipelineStages`. Export a function `getStageOrder(customStages)` that returns the ordered stage names.

The `candidate_stages.stage` column stores the stage name as text. This already works with custom stages since it's freeform text.

### Update KanbanBoard.tsx

Remove the hardcoded `STAGE_CONFIG` map. Accept stages as props (already does via `stages` prop). The color/label info should come from the `pipeline_stages` data.

Change `STAGE_CONFIG` to be dynamic: accept a `stageConfig` prop that maps stage names to `{ label, color, bg }`:
```typescript
interface StageConfig {
  label: string;
  color: string; // hex
  bg: string; // tailwind bg class
}
```

Generate Tailwind-compatible classes from hex colors using opacity variants.

### Update SharedPortal.tsx

Replace hardcoded `STAGE_LABELS` and `STAGE_COLORS` maps. The guest-portal edge function should return stage configs alongside candidates. Or, use a generic display: capitalize the stage name and use a neutral color for unknown stages.

### Integration

- KanbanBoard receives stages from `usePipelineStages` instead of hardcoded constant
- JobDetailView passes custom stages to KanbanBoard
- StageTracker component (if used elsewhere) also uses custom stages
- Team page gets PipelineStageManager section

---

## Feature B: Structured Evaluation Scorecards

### DB Migration (add to same file `20260408800000_custom_stages_and_scorecards.sql`)

```sql
-- Scorecard templates per team
CREATE TABLE public.scorecard_templates (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  criteria jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  -- criteria: [{ id: uuid, label: "Technical Skills", description: "Rate...", max_score: 5 }]
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE public.scorecard_templates ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Team members can view templates" ON public.scorecard_templates FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));
CREATE POLICY "Team admins can manage templates" ON public.scorecard_templates FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id));

-- Scorecard submissions per candidate per evaluator
CREATE TABLE public.scorecard_responses (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  template_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.scorecard_templates(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  resume_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.resumes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  evaluator_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  scores jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  -- scores: { [criteria_id]: { score: 4, comment: "Strong..." } }
  overall_comment text,
  recommendation text CHECK (recommendation IN ('strong_yes', 'yes', 'neutral', 'no', 'strong_no')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE(template_id, resume_id, evaluator_id)
);

ALTER TABLE public.scorecard_responses ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Team members of the job can view/create/update scorecards
CREATE POLICY "Team can view scorecards" ON public.scorecard_responses FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.jobs j LEFT JOIN public.team_members tm ON tm.team_id = j.team_id AND tm.user_id = auth.uid() WHERE j.id = scorecard_responses.job_id AND (j.user_id = auth.uid() OR tm.user_id IS NOT NULL)));

CREATE POLICY "Team can submit scorecards" ON public.scorecard_responses FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (evaluator_id = auth.uid());

CREATE POLICY "Evaluator can update own scorecard" ON public.scorecard_responses FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
  USING (evaluator_id = auth.uid());
```

### Scorecard Template Manager — `src/components/ScorecardTemplateManager.tsx`

Available from Team page or job settings. Lets admins create evaluation templates.

Features:
- List of templates with name and criteria count
- Create template: name + add criteria rows
  - Each criterion: label (e.g., "Technical Skills"), description ("Rate the candidate's..."), max score (1-10, default 5)
  - Add/remove/reorder criteria
- Edit/delete templates
- Common presets: "Technical Interview", "Culture Fit", "Take-Home Assessment"

### Scorecard Submission — `src/components/candidate/ScorecardPanel.tsx`

Displayed in the candidate detail view (CandidateDetailSheet or CandidateRow expanded area).

Props: `resumeId: string, jobId: string, teamId: string`

Features:
- Dropdown to select which scorecard template to fill
- For each criterion: star rating (1-5) or slider + optional comment
- Overall comment textarea
- Recommendation: radio buttons (Strong Yes / Yes / Neutral / No / Strong No) with color coding
- Submit button → saves to `scorecard_responses`
- If current user already submitted for this template+resume, show their existing scores (editable)

### Scorecard Summary — `src/components/candidate/ScorecardSummary.tsx`

Shows aggregate scores across all evaluators for a candidate.

Props: `resumeId: string, jobId: string`

Features:
- Shows how many team members have evaluated
- Per-criterion: average score across evaluators, individual scores
- Overall recommendation distribution (3 Strong Yes, 1 Yes, etc.)
- Compact view for candidate list, expanded for detail sheet

### Integration

- Add `ScorecardPanel` to `CandidateDetailSheet.tsx` — new section below notes
- Add `ScorecardSummary` to `CandidateRow.tsx` expanded view (compact mode)
- Add `ScorecardTemplateManager` to Team page
- Show scorecard completion status on KanbanBoard cards (e.g., "2/3 evaluated" badge)

---

## Constraints
- NEVER edit `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts`
- `(supabase as any)` for new tables
- `@/` imports, shadcn-ui only, Sonner toasts
- Run `npm run build` — zero TypeScript errors

1	# Instant Resume Ranker (Rankora)
2	
3	AI-powered resume screening SaaS. Users paste a job description, upload resumes, and the system scores/ranks candidates using GPT-4o.
4	
5	## Stack
6

9	- **State:** React Query 5 (server state), React Hook Form + Zod (forms)
10	- **Backend:** Supabase (PostgreSQL + Auth + Edge Functions + Storage)
11	- **AI:** OpenAI GPT-4o (resume analysis, JD parsing, scoring)
12	- **Payments:** Dodo Payments (subscriptions + one-time credit packs, hosted checkout)
13	- **Email:** Resend (transactional notifications) + inbound webhook (resume ingestion)

99	
100	## Database Models (Supabase/PostgreSQL)
101	
102	- **profiles** — user_id, credits, plan, inbox_email, email_enabled
103	- **jobs** — user_id, job_description, title, status (pending|processing|completed|failed), scoring weights (must/nice/optional), jd_analysis_json, dynamic_weights_json, jd_embedding (vector)
104	- **resumes** — job_id, filename, file_path, candidate_name, status (pending|done|failed), parsed_json, parsed_text, embedding (vector)
105	- **results** — resume_id, job_id, overall_score, skill_score, experience_score, education_score, missing_skills[], red_flags, matched_must_haves, missing_must_haves, category_scores_json, confidence, hard_fit, strengths_json, gaps_json, explanation_json, interview_questions[]
106	- **users / user_roles** — auth + role enum (admin|user), helper: has_role(), is_job_owner()
107	- **plans** — name, price, credits, billing_type, dodo_product_id, active
108	- **credit_packs** — name, price, credits, active, is_trial, dodo_product_id, dodo_credit_entitlement_id
109	- **payments** — user_id, amount, credits_purchased, status, dodo_payment_id
110	- **feature_flags** — key (unique), enabled, label, description, value_json, category
111	- **platform_config** — singleton: max_resumes_per_job, max_file_size_mb, resume_retention_days, email_ingestion_enabled, payg_per_resume_cost
112	- **ranking_config** — system prompt, model name, temperature, weights
113	- **seo_settings / seo_pages** — meta tags, OG, structured data, analytics
114	- **email_templates** — customizable outbound emails
115	- **admin_audit_logs** — admin_user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, details
116	- **feedback / score_versions** — model evaluation data
117	- **email_ingest_logs** — user_id, job_id, sender, status, attachments_count
118	- **usage_logs** — user_id, job_id, credits_used
119	- **subscription_webhooks** — Dodo Payments webhook audit trail
120	
121	## Component Dependency Map
122	
123	```
124	App.tsx → AuthProvider → QueryClientProvider → BrowserRouter
125	├── Index.tsx
126	│   ├── AppHeader (useAuth, useNavigate)
127	│   ├── JobSidebar (pastJobs[], selectedJobId, onSelectJob, onDeleteJob)
128	│   ├── JobDetailView (useAuth, usePlatformConfig, useFeatureFlags)
129	│   │   ├── ScoreSummaryCards (results[])
130	│   │   ├── CandidateRow (result, resume, expanded, onToggle)
131	│   │   └── AuthDialog → AuthForm
132	│   └── AuthDialog
133	├── Auth.tsx → AppHeader, AuthForm
134	├── Settings.tsx → AppHeader, AccountInfoCard, EmailInboxCard, ChangePasswordCard, UsageHistoryCard, PaymentHistoryCard
135	├── Admin.tsx → AppHeader, AdminSidebar, [DashboardTab|UsersTab|BillingTab|...]
136	└── NotFound.tsx
137	```
138	
139	## Architecture Rules
140	
141	1. **Auth-first:** All data access uses Supabase RLS policies. Never bypass auth.
142	2. **shadcn-ui only:** Use components from `src/components/ui/`. No other UI libraries.
143	3. **Path aliases:** Always import with `@/` prefix (maps to `src/`).
144	4. **React Query:** All server state via React Query hooks. No raw `useEffect` for data fetching.
145	5. **Single Supabase client:** Import from `@/integrations/supabase/client.ts`. Never create new clients.
146	6. **Edge Functions:** Business logic in Supabase Edge Functions (Deno). Frontend calls via `supabase.functions.invoke()`.
147	7. **Credits system:** All ranking operations deduct credits via `deduct_credits()` DB function.
148	8. **Admin audit:** Log all admin mutations via `logAuditAction()` from `@/lib/auditLog.ts`.
149	9. **No hardcoded secrets:** All keys via environment variables (VITE_ prefix for frontend).
150	10. **Auto-generated types:** `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` is auto-generated. Do not manually edit.
151	11. **Sonner toasts:** Use `toast.success()`, `toast.error()` from sonner. No other notification system.
152	12. **Error handling:** Try-catch with toast for user-facing errors. Validation errors as arrays displayed inline.
153	13. **Real-time subscriptions:** Feature flags and SEO settings use Supabase real-time subscriptions + React Query invalidation.
154	
155	## Key Data Flows
156	
157	### Resume Ranking Pipeline
158	```
159	User enters JD + uploads files
160	→ validateFields() checks input
161	→ Create job record (status: pending)
162	→ analyzeJd() → analyze-jd edge function → stores jd_analysis_json
163	→ uploadFilesFromSnapshot() → Supabase Storage + resume records
164	→ rank-resumes edge function (GPT-4o scoring, skill matching)
165	→ rankAndPoll() polls job.status every 2s (max 60 iterations)
166	→ Fetch results from results table
167	→ Merge with resume data, sort by overall_score desc
168	→ Display ScoreSummaryCards + CandidateRow list
169	→ refreshProfile() updates credit count
170	```
171	
172	### Credit System
173	```
174	Check profiles.credits ≥ required
175	→ deduct_credits(user_id, amount) [atomic DB function]
176	→ Log to usage_logs
177	→ Proceed with AI operation
178	→ On failure: no auto-refund (credits already deducted)
179	```
180	
181	### Payment Flows
182	```
183	One-time: BuyCreditsDialog → create-dodo-checkout → redirect to Dodo hosted checkout → dodo-webhook → add credits → PaymentCallback verifies
184	Subscription: SubscriptionDialog → create-dodo-checkout (subscription product) → Dodo checkout → dodo-webhook → update plan+credits
185	Cancellation: cancel-dodo-subscription → plan active until subscription_ends_at → check-expired-subscriptions (cron) → downgrade to free
186	```
187	
188	## Known Code Patterns
189	
190	- **Polling pattern:** `rankAndPoll()` in JobDetailView uses setInterval with iteration counter
191	- **Ref tracking:** `rankingFilesRef` and `resultsRef` track state outside React lifecycle
192	- **Feature flag defaults:** `useFeatureFlag()` returns `enabled: false` before loading (race condition potential)
193	- **SEO type workaround:** `(supabase as any)` cast for seo_settings/seo_pages (not in auto-generated types)
194	- **Dodo hosted checkout:** Both BuyCreditsDialog and SubscriptionDialog use create-dodo-checkout for redirect-based payment
195	- **Admin section mapping:** `sectionComponents` object in Admin.tsx maps section names to components
196	
197	## Commands
198	
199	```bash
200	npm install          # Install dependencies
201	npm run dev          # Start dev server (localhost:8080)
202	npm run build        # Production build
203	npm run test         # Run tests (Vitest)
204	npm run test:watch   # Watch mode tests
205	npx eslint .         # Lint
206	
207	# Supabase
208	supabase functions deploy <name>
209	supabase db push
210	supabase gen types typescript --project-id zkzontawprihrzpayeam > src/integrations/supabase/types.ts
211	```
212	
213	## Safety Rules (CRITICAL)
214	
215	1. **NEVER delete or overwrite existing data/files without explicit user request**
216	2. **NEVER modify payment/billing logic without careful review** — broken payments = lost revenue
217	3. **NEVER change RLS policies without understanding the full security impact**
218	4. **NEVER modify `types.ts`** — it is auto-generated
219	5. **NEVER hardcode API keys, URLs with secrets, or credentials**
220	6. **ALWAYS run `npm run build` after changes to verify no type errors**
221	7. **ALWAYS preserve existing error handling** — do not remove try-catch blocks
222	8. **ALWAYS maintain backward compatibility** — existing API contracts must not break
223	9. **When in doubt, ask the user** — never guess about business logic
224

# Plan: Custom Pipeline Stages + Structured Evaluation Scorecards

## Task
Build two features for Rankora:
- Feature A: Custom Pipeline Stages (per-team configurable Kanban stages)
- Feature B: Structured Evaluation Scorecards (template-based candidate scoring)

## Context Verified
- Stack: React 18.3 + Vite + TypeScript + shadcn/ui + React Query 5 + Supabase
- Dev port: 8080
- `(supabase as any)` cast for new tables (not in types.ts)
- Sonner toasts only
- `@/` imports throughout
- `is_team_member()` and `is_team_admin()` SQL functions already exist
- Teams table and team_members table already exist with owner/admin/member roles
- KanbanBoard already accepts `stages: string[]` prop — partially stage-agnostic
- StageTracker component is tightly coupled to hardcoded STAGE_ORDER
- `effectiveStageCounts` in JobDetailView is hardcoded to 6 fixed stages
- CandidateDetailSheet has section ordering: StageTracker → Notes → AI panels
- Team page at `/team` (src/pages/Team.tsx) — good place to add PipelineStageManager
- Migration file will be: `supabase/migrations/20260408800000_custom_stages_and_scorecards.sql`

## What Exists (Do Not Break)
- `src/hooks/useStageTracker.ts` — exports `HiringStage`, `STAGE_ORDER`, `useStages`, `useUpdateStage`, `useStageSummary`
- `src/components/KanbanBoard.tsx` — already accepts `stages: string[]`, STAGE_CONFIG is internal
- `src/components/candidate/StageTracker.tsx` — imports `STAGE_ORDER` from useStageTracker, renders dots
- `src/components/CandidateRow.tsx` — has `STAGE_BADGE_CLASSES` hardcoded map
- `src/pages/SharedPortal.tsx` — has `STAGE_LABELS` and `STAGE_COLORS` hardcoded
- `src/components/JobDetailView.tsx` — uses `STAGE_ORDER` for kanban, `effectiveStageCounts` hardcoded
- Existing migration files through `20260408700000_enhance_career_settings.sql`

## Risk Assessment
1. Risk: Breaking `StageTracker.tsx` and `CandidateDetailSheet.tsx` which use `HiringStage` type
   Mitigation: Keep `HiringStage` type and `STAGE_ORDER` in useStageTracker.ts as-is (backward compat). New `usePipelineStages` hook is additive only.

2. Risk: `effectiveStageCounts` in JobDetailView is hardcoded to 6 fixed stage names
   Mitigation: Update it to derive counts from custom stages dynamically; keep "rejected" special.

3. Risk: KanbanBoard's mobile `<select>` uses `STAGE_CONFIG[s]?.label` to get display labels  
   Mitigation: Add `stageConfig` prop to KanbanBoard for display overrides; keep fallback to capitalize.

## Files to Create

### New files:
1. `supabase/migrations/20260408800000_custom_stages_and_scorecards.sql`
2. `src/hooks/usePipelineStages.tsx`
3. `src/hooks/useScorecardTemplates.tsx`
4. `src/hooks/useScorecardResponses.tsx`
5. `src/components/PipelineStageManager.tsx`
6. `src/components/ScorecardTemplateManager.tsx`
7. `src/components/candidate/ScorecardPanel.tsx`
8. `src/components/candidate/ScorecardSummary.tsx`

### Files to modify:
9. `src/components/KanbanBoard.tsx` — add optional `stageConfig` prop for labels/colors
10. `src/components/JobDetailView.tsx` — wire usePipelineStages, update effectiveStageCounts
11. `src/components/candidate/StageTracker.tsx` — accept optional custom stages prop
12. `src/components/CandidateDetailSheet.tsx` — add ScorecardPanel below Notes
13. `src/pages/Team.tsx` — add PipelineStageManager + ScorecardTemplateManager sections
14. `src/pages/SharedPortal.tsx` — make stage display generic (capitalize, neutral colors)

## Implementation Plan (Step-by-Step)

### Step 1: DB Migration
Create `supabase/migrations/20260408800000_custom_stages_and_scorecards.sql`
- `pipeline_stages` table (id, team_id FK teams, name, color, sort_order, is_default, created_at)
- RLS: team members SELECT, team admins ALL
- Seed default stages for existing teams
- `scorecard_templates` table (id, team_id FK teams, name, criteria JSONB, created_at)
- RLS: team members SELECT, team admins ALL
- `scorecard_responses` table (id, template_id FK, resume_id FK, job_id FK, evaluator_id FK auth.users, scores JSONB, overall_comment, recommendation CHECK, created_at, updated_at, UNIQUE(template_id, resume_id, evaluator_id))
- RLS: team members of the job SELECT, authenticated INSERT (evaluator_id = auth.uid()), evaluator UPDATE own

### Step 2: usePipelineStages hook
Create `src/hooks/usePipelineStages.tsx`
- Query pipeline_stages for teamId ordered by sort_order
- Append synthetic "rejected" entry (not stored in DB, always last)
- If no custom stages (or null teamId), return DEFAULT_STAGES as fallback
- Mutations: createStage, updateStage, deleteStage, reorderStages
- Realtime subscription on pipeline_stages table

Types exported:
```typescript
export interface PipelineStage {
  id: string;
  team_id: string;
  name: string;
  color: string;
  sort_order: number;
  is_default: boolean;
}
export const DEFAULT_STAGES: PipelineStage[] = [...] // matches hardcoded STAGE_ORDER
```

### Step 3: useScorecardTemplates hook
Create `src/hooks/useScorecardTemplates.tsx`
- Query scorecard_templates for teamId
- Mutations: createTemplate, updateTemplate, deleteTemplate

Types:
```typescript
export interface ScorecardCriterion { id: string; label: string; description: string; max_score: number; }
export interface ScorecardTemplate { id: string; team_id: string; name: string; criteria: ScorecardCriterion[]; created_at: string; }
```

### Step 4: useScorecardResponses hook
Create `src/hooks/useScorecardResponses.tsx`
- Query scorecard_responses for resumeId + jobId
- Mutations: submitResponse (upsert), updateResponse

Types:
```typescript
export type Recommendation = 'strong_yes' | 'yes' | 'neutral' | 'no' | 'strong_no';
export interface ScorecardResponse { id: string; template_id: string; resume_id: string; job_id: string; evaluator_id: string; scores: Record<string, { score: number; comment?: string }>; overall_comment?: string; recommendation?: Recommendation; }
```

### Step 5: PipelineStageManager component
Create `src/components/PipelineStageManager.tsx`
Props: `teamId: string`

UI:
- Header: "Pipeline Stages" title + "Add Stage" button
- List of stages: colored dot, name, reorder (up/down arrows), edit, delete
- Add/edit inline form: name input + color picker (6 preset colors as swatches)
- Cannot delete if isDefault or name === "Rejected" or total ≤ 2
- On delete: confirm AlertDialog
- Save reorder on each up/down click (immediate mutation)
- Uses usePipelineStages hook

### Step 6: Update KanbanBoard.tsx
Add optional `stageConfig` prop:
```typescript
interface StageDisplayConfig {
  label: string;
  color?: string; // hex
}
interface KanbanBoardProps {
  // existing props...
  stageConfig?: Record<string, StageDisplayConfig>;
}
```
- getStageConfig(): first checks `stageConfig` prop, falls back to hardcoded STAGE_CONFIG, then generic fallback
- Mobile `<select>` option labels use stageConfig prop labels
- Keep STAGE_CONFIG as internal fallback (backward compat, no removal)

### Step 7: Update StageTracker.tsx
Add optional props for custom stages:
```typescript
interface StageTrackerProps {
  currentStage: string; // was HiringStage — widen to string
  updatedAt?: string | null;
  onStageChange: (stage: string) => void;
  disabled?: boolean;
  customStages?: Array<{ name: string; label: string }>; // if provided, renders these instead of STAGE_ORDER
}
```
- If `customStages` provided, iterate those instead of STAGE_ORDER
- Keep HiringStage import for backward compat
- currentStage widened to string (still accepts HiringStage values)

### Step 8: Update JobDetailView.tsx
- Import `usePipelineStages` hook
- Call `usePipelineStages(team?.id ?? null)` to get custom stages
- Pass `stageConfig` to KanbanBoard derived from pipeline stages data
- Update `stages={[...STAGE_ORDER, "rejected"]}` to use custom stage names
- Update `effectiveStageCounts` to be dynamic based on custom stages
- Update `stageFilter` type from `HiringStage | null` to `string | null`
- Pass custom stages to StageTracker via CandidateDetailSheet props

### Step 9: Update CandidateDetailSheet.tsx
- Add `teamId?: string | null` prop
- Add `customStages?: PipelineStage[]` prop
- Pass customStages to StageTracker component
- Add ScorecardPanel below Notes section (requires resumeId, jobId, teamId)

### Step 10: ScorecardTemplateManager component
Create `src/components/ScorecardTemplateManager.tsx`
Props: `teamId: string`

UI:
- Header: "Evaluation Scorecards" title + "New Template" button
- List of templates: name, criteria count, edit/delete buttons
- Edit view (inline expand or same-area form):
  - Template name input
  - Criteria list: each row has label input, description input, max_score select (1-10)
  - Add/remove criteria buttons
  - Reorder criteria (up/down)
  - Preset buttons: "Technical Interview" | "Culture Fit" | "Take-Home Assessment"
  - Save / Cancel buttons
- Delete: AlertDialog confirmation
- Uses useScorecardTemplates hook

### Step 11: ScorecardPanel component
Create `src/components/candidate/ScorecardPanel.tsx`
Props: `resumeId: string, jobId: string, teamId: string | null`

UI:
- Header: "Evaluations" with count badge
- Template selector dropdown (from useScorecardTemplates)
- If no templates: "No scorecard templates yet. Create one in Team Settings." link
- For selected template, show:
  - Each criterion: label + description + star rating (1-5, or up to max_score) + optional comment textarea
  - Overall comment textarea
  - Recommendation radio: Strong Yes / Yes / Neutral / No / Strong No (color coded)
  - Submit/Update button (disabled while pending)
- If current user already submitted: load their existing response pre-filled (editable)
- Uses useScorecardTemplates + useScorecardResponses hooks

### Step 12: ScorecardSummary component
Create `src/components/candidate/ScorecardSummary.tsx`
Props: `resumeId: string, jobId: string, compact?: boolean`

UI (compact for CandidateRow, full for CandidateDetailSheet):
- Compact: "N evaluated" badge with recommendation breakdown as colored dots
- Full:
  - "X of Y team members evaluated" header
  - Per-criterion average score bar
  - Recommendation distribution: "3 Strong Yes, 1 Yes" etc.
  - Individual evaluator score breakdown (anonymous or by initial)

### Step 13: Update Team.tsx
- Import PipelineStageManager + ScorecardTemplateManager
- Add two new Card sections after existing team management cards:
  1. Pipeline Stages section with PipelineStageManager (only if team exists)
  2. Evaluation Scorecards section with ScorecardTemplateManager (only if team exists)
- Show role gate: only show management UI if myRole is "owner" or "admin"

### Step 14: Update SharedPortal.tsx
- Replace hardcoded `STAGE_LABELS[stage] ?? stage` with `stage.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + stage.slice(1)` for unknown stages
- Replace `STAGE_COLORS[stage] ?? "bg-muted text-muted-foreground"` with generic fallback
- Keep existing entries for known stages (backward compat, guest portal doesn't load custom stages)

### Step 15: npm run build — verify zero errors

## Data Flow

### Custom Stages Flow:
Team page → PipelineStageManager → usePipelineStages → pipeline_stages table
JobDetailView → usePipelineStages(team.id) → stages list
→ KanbanBoard (stages=[...stageNames], stageConfig={name→label+color})
→ StageTracker (customStages=[{name, label}])
candidate_stages.stage column stores raw stage name text (already freeform)

### Scorecard Flow:
Team page → ScorecardTemplateManager → useScorecardTemplates → scorecard_templates table
CandidateDetailSheet → ScorecardPanel → useScorecardTemplates + useScorecardResponses
→ scorecard_responses table (UNIQUE constraint prevents duplicates per evaluator per resume per template)
CandidateDetailSheet → ScorecardSummary (aggregate view)

## Edge Cases Handled
- No team: usePipelineStages returns DEFAULT_STAGES (hardcoded fallback = current behavior)
- No custom stages in DB: same fallback
- "Rejected" is always synthetic (never in pipeline_stages table, always appended)
- Cannot delete below 2 stages (guard in PipelineStageManager)
- Scorecard template has no criteria: UI shows empty state inside ScorecardPanel
- Evaluator submits scorecard twice: UNIQUE constraint in DB → upsert handles update
- CustomStages unknown in StageTracker: widened to string, dots render for each custom stage

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Team admins can create/edit/delete/reorder pipeline stages from Team page
- [ ] KanbanBoard uses custom stage names and colors when team has custom stages
- [ ] StageTracker renders custom stages (not hardcoded 5 stages) when custom stages provided
- [ ] Default fallback still works for users without teams or without custom stages
- [ ] Team admins can create scorecard templates with criteria from Team page
- [ ] Evaluators can submit scorecards from CandidateDetailSheet (ScorecardPanel)
- [ ] ScorecardSummary shows aggregated scores per candidate
- [ ] npm run build exits with 0 errors

**`pipeline_stages`** — per-team, ordered by `sort_order`. RLS: members read, admins write. Seeded with 5 defaults for existing teams.

**`scorecard_templates`** — criteria stored as JSONB array `[{id, label, description, max_score}]`. RLS: members read, admins write.

**`scorecard_responses`** — UNIQUE on `(template_id, resume_id, evaluator_id)` so upsert handles edits. Scores as JSONB `{criteria_id: {score, comment}}`. Recommendation as CHECK enum.

---

### Risk Mitigations

- `StageTracker` currently renders `STAGE_ORDER.length` (5) dots — after change it renders `customStages.length` or falls back to STAGE_ORDER when no prop passed
- `effectiveStageCounts` is currently typed `Record<HiringStage, number>` — will change to `Record<string, number>` with dynamic keys from custom stages
